answer.question: A friend is helping me apartment-hunt and found two listings in Ashford Heights: Option A is a second-floor unit on a busy commercial avenue with large street-facing windows and below-market rent, and Option B is a third-floor unit on a residential side street with a balcony overlooking an interior garden but costs 15% more. Based on everything you know about my living situation history and what matters to me, draft a short recommendation with your reasoning.
answer.expected_answer: I'd recommend Option B — the third-floor unit on the residential side street with the interior garden balcony. Your housing history shows that quiet and peacefulness are your top priorities: you left your previous apartment at 118 Caldwell Street specifically because of unbearable street noise that ruined your sleep, and when choosing your current place at 742 Birchwood Lane you deliberately selected the unit with a courtyard-facing balcony over a street-facing one, even confirming the orientation with the landlord before signing. You also built a cherished morning coffee routine in the quiet enclosed courtyard. Option A's busy commercial avenue and large street-facing windows would recreate exactly the conditions that made your Caldwell Street experience miserable. The 15% premium for Option B is justified given that noise avoidance is your primary housing criterion — you've demonstrated you'll prioritize quiet over cost savings.
answer.gold_memory_state: Confirmed current address: 742 Birchwood Lane, Unit 3B, Ashford Heights (60143). Previous address: 118 Caldwell Street, Apartment 12, Maplewood — left due to unbearable noise. Balcony orientation: chose courtyard-facing over street-facing. Morning routine: quiet courtyard coffee. Synthesized preference: quiet/peaceful living is the top housing priority; noise avoidance is primary criterion. Tentative Unit 4A not yet finalized. Mother's address: 4010 Greenleaf Boulevard, Westbrook (unrelated to recommendation).
